paper_title: Measurement-induced entanglement and complexity in random constant-depth 2D quantum circuits (McGinley, 2025, arXiv)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.} The replica-free entanglement-of-assistance pipeline gives the finite-size theorem
\[
F_{\mathrm{SAW}}:=-\log Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}\ge 2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
E(A:C):=\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})
\ge 2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}-2\log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}).
\]
Here
\[
Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}=\sum_{W\in \operatorname{SAW}(\Lambda^*,A,C)}\exp[-S_W^{(2)}/2].
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & E(A:C)=S(A\mid M_B)_\rho.\\
(P2) & E(A:C)\ge (1-\epsilon/2)\log d'-h_2(\epsilon/2).\\
(P3) & \epsilon=\left\|\sum_{I\subseteq B}
(\Theta_A\otimes \Theta_I\otimes \widehat D_{B\setminus I}\otimes \operatorname{Tr}_C)[\Psi^{ABC}]
\right\|_1.\\
(P4) & \text{For each separating wall }W,\quad
\|X(I_W)\|_1\le \exp\{(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})/2\}.\\
(P5) & \text{After grouping configurations by their nonempty set of separating walls,}\\
     & \epsilon\le \sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}f(Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}),\qquad f(x):=(e^x-1)/x.\\
(P6) & F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-\log Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}\ge 2.\\
(P7) & \lceil a\rceil\le 2a\text{ for }a\ge 1,\quad e^y-1\le ye^y\text{ for }y\ge 0.\\
(P8) & h_2\text{ is increasing on }[0,1/2]\text{ and }h_2(y)\le 2y\log(1/y)\text{ for }0<y\le 1/2.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Premises (P3)--(P5) are the point at which the local measurement problem is converted into a self-avoiding-walk partition function: the subset expansion labels Ising configurations, (P4) gives the cost of forcing a particular separating wall, and the inclusion-exclusion grouping of one or more walls gives the exponential series in (P5).

Set $F:=F_{\mathrm{SAW}}$ and choose
\[
d'=\left\lceil F^{-2}e^{2F}\right\rceil .
\]
Since $F\ge 2$, the number $F^{-2}e^{2F}$ is at least $1$.  Therefore
\begin{align}
\sqrt{d'}
&\le \sqrt{2F^{-2}e^{2F}} && \text{by (P7)}\\
&=\sqrt 2\,F^{-1}e^F. && \text{algebra}
\end{align}
Because $Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}=e^{-F}$, premise (P5) gives
\begin{align}
\epsilon
&\le \sqrt{d'}\,e^{-F}f(e^{-F})\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\,(e^{e^{-F}}-1) && \text{definition of }f\\
&\le \sqrt 2\,F^{-1}e^F\,e^{-F}e^{e^{-F}} && \text{by (P7)}\\
&=\sqrt 2\,F^{-1}e^{e^{-F}}\\
&\le 2F^{-1}, && \text{since }F\ge 2.
\end{align}
Hence
\[
0\le \epsilon/2\le 1/F\le 1/2.
\]
Using (P8),
\begin{align}
h_2(\epsilon/2)
&\le h_2(1/F)\\
&\le 2F^{-1}\log F.
\end{align}
Also, from the definition of $d'$,
\begin{align}
\log d'
&\ge \log(F^{-2}e^{2F})\\
&=2F-2\log F.
\end{align}
Substitution into the one-shot distillation lower bound gives
\begin{align}
E(A:C)
&\ge (1-\epsilon/2)\log d'-h_2(\epsilon/2) && \text{by (P2)}\\
&\ge (1-F^{-1})(2F-2\log F)-2F^{-1}\log F\\
&=2F-2\log F-2\\
&=2F-2\log(eF).
\end{align}
Finally, by (P1), this lower bound is exactly a lower bound on the average post-measurement entanglement entropy.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
F_{\mathrm{SAW}}\ge 2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})
\ge 2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}-2\log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}).
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.} The finite-size theorem becomes an extensive measurement-induced-entanglement phase for exactly the three architecture families specified in the paper: holographic tensor-network circuits with $S_e^{(2)}>2\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}$, depth-$2$ four-local plaquette circuits with $q\ge 88$, and depth-$4$ two-local brickwork circuits with $q\ge 134$.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & E(A:C)\ge 2F-2\log(eF)\text{ whenever }F\ge 2.\\
(P2) & \text{Every separating wall has length }\ell\ge L_x.\\
(P3) & \text{The number of separating walks of length }\ell\text{ is at most }L_y\mu^\ell.\\
(P4) & L_y\le L_x^a\text{ for some fixed }a>0.\\
(P5) & \text{If }Z\le C L_y e^{-mL_x}\text{ for constants }C>0,m>0,\text{ then }F=-\log Z.\\
(P6) & \text{Holographic family: }H(W)=S_e^{(2)}|W|/2,\quad \mu=\mu_{\Lambda^*}.\\
(P7) & \text{Plaquette family: the }8\times 4\text{ cell enumeration defines a decreasing factor }g_P(q),\\
     & \text{built from }c_1(q)^2=q(q+1)/(q^4+1)\text{ and }c_2(q)^2=2q^2/(q^4+1),\\
     & \text{and }q\ge 88\text{ implies }\mu_{\mathrm{hex}}g_P(q)\le e^{-\eta_P}\text{ for some }\eta_P>0.\\
(P8) & \text{Brickwork family: the }8\times 4\text{ cell enumeration defines a decreasing factor }g_B(q),\\
     & \text{built from }c'_1(q)^2=q(q^4+6q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^3,\ c'_2(q)=2q/(q^2+1),\\
     & \text{and split-pair factors bounded by }\sqrt 3/q,\\
     & \text{with }q\ge 134\text{ implying }\mu_{\mathrm{hex}}g_B(q)\le e^{-\eta_B}\text{ for some }\eta_B>0.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First prove the common asymptotic extraction.  Suppose
\[
Z\le C L_y e^{-mL_x}
\]
for fixed $C>0$ and $m>0$.  Then
\begin{align}
F
&=-\log Z && \text{by (P5)}\\
&\ge mL_x-\log L_y-\log C\\
&\ge mL_x-a\log L_x-\log C && \text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
Thus $F\ge 2$ for all sufficiently large $L_x$, and (P1) gives
\begin{align}
E(A:C)
&\ge 2F-2\log(eF)\\
&\ge 2mL_x-2a\log L_x-2\log C-2\log(eF).
\end{align}
The last three terms are $o(L_x)$ in the polynomial-width regime.  Therefore, for every $0<\kappa<2m$, there is $L_0$ such that
\[
L_x\ge L_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E(A:C)\ge \kappa L_x.
\]

For the holographic family, set
\[
\beta:=S_e^{(2)}/2.
\]
Choose any $\eta$ satisfying $0<\eta<\beta-\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}$.  The connective-constant counting bound gives, for all sufficiently large lengths,
\[
\#\{W:|W|=\ell\}\le L_y\exp[(\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}+\eta)\ell].
\]
Using $H(W)=\beta |W|$,
\begin{align}
Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}
&=\sum_W e^{-\beta |W|}\\
&\le L_y\sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}\exp[-(\beta-\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}-\eta)\ell]\\
&=\frac{L_y e^{-m_HL_x}}{1-e^{-m_H}},
\end{align}
where
\[
m_H:=\beta-\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}-\eta>0.
\]
The common extraction gives every
\[
0<\kappa<2m_H=S_e^{(2)}-2\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}-2\eta.
\]
Since $\eta$ can be arbitrarily small, every $\kappa<S_e^{(2)}-2\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}$ is obtained.

For the depth-$2$ plaquette family, the finite cell enumeration in (P7) replaces $e^{-H(W)}$ by the cell weight $g_P(q)^{|W|}$.  Hence
\begin{align}
Z_P
&\le \sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}L_y\mu_{\mathrm{hex}}^\ell g_P(q)^\ell && \text{by (P2), (P3), (P7)}\\
&\le L_y\sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}e^{-\eta_P\ell}\\
&=\frac{L_y e^{-\eta_P L_x}}{1-e^{-\eta_P}}.
\end{align}
Thus the common extraction applies with $m=\eta_P$ and gives
\[
\mathbb E_U E(A:C)\ge \kappa_P L_x
\]
for some $\kappa_P>0$ and all sufficiently large $L_x$.

For the depth-$4$ brickwork family, the compilation into blocked plaquette-like cells and the enumeration in (P8) give the analogous bound
\begin{align}
Z_B
&\le \sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}L_y\mu_{\mathrm{hex}}^\ell g_B(q)^\ell\\
&\le L_y\sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}e^{-\eta_B\ell}\\
&=\frac{L_y e^{-\eta_B L_x}}{1-e^{-\eta_B}}.
\end{align}
The common extraction applies with $m=\eta_B$ and gives
\[
\mathbb E_U E(A:C)\ge \kappa_B L_x
\]
for some $\kappa_B>0$ and all sufficiently large $L_x$.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
S_e^{(2)}>2\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}
\Longrightarrow
\mathbb E_U E(A:C)\ge \kappa L_x
\text{ for every }0<\kappa<S_e^{(2)}-2\log\mu_{\Lambda^*}.
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
q\ge 88\Longrightarrow \mathbb E_U E(A:C)\ge \kappa_P L_x,\qquad
q\ge 134\Longrightarrow \mathbb E_U E(A:C)\ge \kappa_B L_x.
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.} In the square-lattice holographic and random-tensor-network regimes specified by the paper, the ordered self-avoiding-walk phase forces column-wise MPS boundary algorithms to abort with probability at least $1-\exp[-\Omega(\sqrt N)]$.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \xi:=\min(t,L_x/2)\text{ is the distance scale crossed by the relevant separating wall.}\\
(P2) & \mathbb E_U[\epsilon_\xi]\le \sqrt{d'}e^{-m\xi}\text{ for some constant }m>0.\\
(P3) & \Pr_{s_B,U}\!\left(S(\rho^A_{s_B})<\log d'-2\log 2\right)
        \le \frac12\mathbb E_U[\epsilon_\xi]\log d'.\\
(P4) & d'=e^{\alpha\xi}\text{ with }0<\alpha<2m.\\
(P5) & \text{For a square }L_x\times L_x\text{ system, }N=L_x^2\text{ and one may take }\xi=L_x/2.\\
(P6) & \text{An exact MPS with bond dimension }D\text{ has half-chain entropy at most }\log D.\\
(P7) & \text{The bounded-error boundary-state approximation criterion used by }\mathsf{SEBD}\text{ and }\mathsf{bMPS}\\
     & \text{requires }D=\exp[\Omega(\xi)]\text{ on the high-entropy states produced here.}\\
(P8) & \text{A polynomial cap has }D\le N^b\text{ for some fixed }b,\text{ hence }\log D=O(\log N).\\
(P9) & \text{The algorithm aborts whenever no boundary MPS within the cap satisfies its error criterion.}\\
(P10)& S_e^{(2)}>2.8\text{ bits puts the square-lattice holographic }\mathsf{SEBD}\text{ instance in the ordered regime.}\\
(P11)& \text{For maximally entangled bonds, }S_e^{(2)}=\log_2\chi;\ \chi\ge 7\text{ implies }\log_2\chi>2.8.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
By (P2) and (P4),
\begin{align}
\mathbb E_U[\epsilon_\xi]
&\le \sqrt{d'}e^{-m\xi}\\
&=e^{\alpha\xi/2}e^{-m\xi}\\
&=e^{-(m-\alpha/2)\xi}.
\end{align}
Let
\[
c:=m-\alpha/2>0.
\]
Then (P3) gives
\begin{align}
\Pr_{s_B,U}\!\left(S(\rho^A_{s_B})<\log d'-2\log 2\right)
&\le \frac12 e^{-c\xi}\alpha\xi\\
&=\exp[-\Omega(\xi)].
\end{align}
Therefore, with probability at least $1-\exp[-\Omega(\xi)]$,
\begin{align}
S(\rho^A_{s_B})
&\ge \log d'-2\log 2\\
&=\alpha\xi-2\log 2\\
&=\Omega(\xi).
\end{align}
Using the square geometry (P5),
\[
\xi=L_x/2=\sqrt N/2,
\]
so
\[
\Pr\!\left(S(\rho^A_{s_B})=\Omega(\sqrt N)\right)
\ge 1-\exp[-\Omega(\sqrt N)].
\]

Now compare this entropy requirement with a polynomial MPS cap.  If $D\le N^b$, then
\begin{align}
\log D&\le b\log N=O(\log N) && \text{by (P8)}.
\end{align}
For exact representation, (P6) contradicts the high-entropy event for all sufficiently large $N$, since
\[
\Omega(\sqrt N)>O(\log N).
\]
For the bounded-error algorithms in the paper, (P7) strengthens the same obstruction: on the high-entropy event the required bond dimension is
\[
D=\exp[\Omega(\xi)]=\exp[\Omega(\sqrt N)],
\]
which exceeds every polynomial cap.  Therefore the abort rule (P9) implies
\[
\Pr(\text{abort})\ge 1-\exp[-\Omega(\sqrt N)].
\]
Premise (P10) identifies the square-lattice holographic circuit regime for \(\mathsf{SEBD}\), and (P11) transfers the same entropy threshold to the random tensor-network contraction setting with maximally entangled bond dimension \(\chi\ge 7\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
S_e^{(2)}>2.8\text{ bits}
\Longrightarrow
\Pr[\mathsf{SEBD}\text{ aborts}]\ge 1-\exp[-\Omega(\sqrt N)].
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
\chi\ge 7
\Longrightarrow
\Pr[\mathsf{bMPS}\text{ aborts}]\ge 1-\exp[-\Omega(\sqrt N)].
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.} For the square-lattice holographic Clifford circuit with local qudit dimension $q=2^m$ and integer $m\ge 6$, there is a constant $\delta>0$ such that every all-to-all probabilistic classical sampler satisfying
\[
\mathbb E_U\operatorname{TV}(Q_U,P_U)\le \delta
\]
has depth $\Omega(\log N)$.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \text{If an ensemble has long-ranged tripartite measurement-induced entanglement with constant probability,}\\
     & \text{then any constant-average-TV classical sampler for it has depth }\Omega(\log N).\\
(P2) & \text{Long-ranged tripartite MIE follows if three well-separated site marginals are non-pure}\\
     & \text{stabilizer marginals with constant probability before the final local Clifford projection.}\\
(P3) & \text{Random output qubits }h,i,j\text{ occupy distinct well-separated sites }H,I,J\text{ with probability }p_{\mathrm{geo}}>0.\\
(P4) & \text{For a stabilizer marginal }\rho_X,\ S(\rho_X)=0\text{ iff }\rho_X\text{ is pure; otherwise }S(\rho_X)\ge \log 2.\\
(P5) & \Pr(\rho_X\text{ is pure})\le \mathbb E[\epsilon_X].\\
(P6) & \mathbb E[\epsilon_X]\le \sqrt 2\,Z_{\mathrm{loop}}f(Z_{\mathrm{loop}}),\quad f(z)=(e^z-1)/z.\\
(P7) & \beta=(m/2)\log 2,\quad \nu=\exp(\log\mu_{\mathrm{sq}}-\beta).\\
(P8) & m\ge 6\text{ implies }\beta\ge \log(3\mu_{\mathrm{sq}})\text{ and hence }\nu\le 1/3.\\
(P9) & \nu\le 1/3\text{ implies }Z_{\mathrm{loop}}\le z_0\text{ for a constant }z_0\\
     & \text{with }\sqrt 2\,z_0f(z_0)<1/3.\\
(P10)& \Pr(A_1\cup A_2\cup A_3)\le \Pr(A_1)+\Pr(A_2)+\Pr(A_3).
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For a fixed site $X\in\{H,I,J\}$, premises (P5)--(P9) imply
\begin{align}
\Pr(\rho_X\text{ is pure})
&\le \mathbb E[\epsilon_X]\\
&\le \sqrt 2\,Z_{\mathrm{loop}}f(Z_{\mathrm{loop}})\\
&\le \sqrt 2\,z_0f(z_0)\\
&<1/3.
\end{align}
Choose $c_3$ such that
\[
\sqrt 2\,z_0f(z_0)\le c_3<1/3.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
\Pr\!\left(\bigcup_{X\in\{H,I,J\}}\{\rho_X\text{ is pure}\}\right)
&\le \sum_{X\in\{H,I,J\}}\Pr(\rho_X\text{ is pure}) && \text{by (P10)}\\
&\le 3c_3\\
&<1.
\end{align}
Thus, conditioned on the well-separated-site event, all three site marginals are non-pure with probability at least $1-3c_3>0$.  By the stabilizer dichotomy (P4),
\[
S(\rho_X)\ge \log 2\qquad\text{for all }X\in\{H,I,J\}
\]
on that event.  Combining with the geometric probability (P3) gives
\[
p_0:=p_{\mathrm{geo}}(1-3c_3)>0
\]
for three well-separated non-pure stabilizer marginals.

By (P2), the final local Clifford projection converts this constant-probability event into the long-ranged tripartite MIE condition with some probability $p_1>0$ independent of $N$.  Therefore the ensemble satisfies the hypothesis of the sampler lower-bound theorem (P1).  Consequently there exists a constant $\delta>0$ such that every probabilistic all-to-all classical circuit family with
\[
\mathbb E_U\operatorname{TV}(Q_U,P_U)\le \delta
\]
must obey
\[
\operatorname{depth}(C_N)=\Omega(\log N).
\]

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
m\ge 6,\ q=2^m,\ \mathbb E_U\operatorname{TV}(Q_U,P_U)\le \delta
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{depth}(C_N)=\Omega(\log N).
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_metadata.revision_intent: Improve alignment by separating the general finite SAW theorem from the architecture-specific extensive-phase proof, and by making the downstream MPS-failure and Clifford-depth arguments more explicit.

rubric_interpretation.format_constraints: The output is exactly one JSON object with paper_title, contiguous deeper_reasoning_k string fields, and one deeper_metadata object; proof strings are LaTeX-compatible with article, amsmath, and amssymb only.
rubric_interpretation.value_constraints: The selected derivations must be theorem-level chains that combine multiple core_reasoning entries into the paper's canonical goal endpoints rather than restating isolated lemmas.
rubric_interpretation.controlled_lemma_policy: Paper-specific finite enumerations and external complexity-theoretic implications are included as controlled premises only where re-deriving them would require reproducing appendices outside the extracted core.

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Finite SAW free-energy theorem for average post-measurement entanglement
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: Directly proves the G1 finite theorem endpoint E(A:C) >= 2F_SAW - 2log(eF_SAW) whenever F_SAW >= 2.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Shows why a 2D measurement problem reduces to a positive free-energy condition for separating self-avoiding walks.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Combines conditional entropy, one-shot distillation, multiparty splitting, wall norm bounds, and rank optimization into a single proof certificate.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: Keeps the F_SAW >= 2 threshold, the ceiling choice for d', the epsilon <= 2/F estimate, and the final logarithmic correction explicit.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejects standalone derivations of only E(A:C)=S(A|M_B) or only the wall norm bound because they do not reach a goal-level endpoint.
controlled_external_lemmas: grouping of nonempty separating-wall collections into the exponential-series factor f(Z_SAW)
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The inclusion-exclusion grouping is stated as a controlled premise but its algebraic consequence is fully propagated through the proof.

deeper_reasoning_2.title: Architecture-specific extensive MIE phase from positive SAW mass
deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: Proves the three G1 extensive-instantiation endpoints: holographic, depth-2 plaquette q>=88, and depth-4 brickwork q>=134.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Identifies the physical ordered phase as strict positivity of a self-avoiding-walk mass after inserting the correct local architecture weights.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Separates the universal asymptotic extraction from the architecture-specific mass certificates and includes the local enumeration factors used to set q thresholds.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: Tracks kappa below S_e^(2)-2log mu for holographic circuits and positive constants eta_P, eta_B for the q-threshold circuit families.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids treating q>=88 and q>=134 as unexplained labels by recording the cell-factor mechanism and local Schatten-2 ingredients.
controlled_external_lemmas: Appendix-E finite enumeration proving mu_hex g_P(q) <= exp(-eta_P) for q>=88
Appendix-E finite enumeration proving mu_hex g_B(q) <= exp(-eta_B) for q>=134
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The finite enumeration itself is not reproduced term by term; the proof includes the operational definition of the factors and uses only their threshold-certified consequences.

deeper_reasoning_3.title: High-probability boundary entropy obstruction to polynomial-bond MPS algorithms
deeper_reasoning_3.goal_alignment: Derives the SEBD and bMPS abort probabilities required by G2, including the S_e^(2)>2.8 and chi>=7 regimes.
deeper_reasoning_3.scientific_payoff: Shows that the same ordered MIE regime that proves macroscopic entanglement also rules out efficient one-dimensional boundary compression.
deeper_reasoning_3.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Turns a distillation-error tail estimate into a high-probability lower bound on required MPS bond dimension, then into algorithm failure.
deeper_reasoning_3.formal_sharpness: Tracks xi, alpha, m, L_x=sqrt(N), exp[-Omega(sqrt(N))], S_e^(2)>2.8 bits, and chi>=7.
deeper_reasoning_3.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejects generic claims that MPS struggle with entanglement; the proof uses the exact scaling mismatch Omega(sqrt(N)) versus O(log N).
controlled_external_lemmas: bounded-error approximation of the boundary states considered requires D=exp[Omega(xi)]
deeper_reasoning_3.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The exact MPS entropy obstruction is derived explicitly; the bounded-error strengthening is declared as a controlled paper-specific lemma.

deeper_reasoning_4.title: Tripartite stabilizer MIE forces logarithmic classical sampler depth
deeper_reasoning_4.goal_alignment: Proves the G3 endpoint that average-TV classical samplers for the q=2^m, m>=6 Clifford ensemble require depth Omega(log N).
deeper_reasoning_4.scientific_payoff: Connects the geometric loop partition bound to a computational lower bound through tripartite measurement-induced stabilizer entanglement.
deeper_reasoning_4.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Makes the m>=6 threshold, loop partition control, non-pure marginal event, and final sampler-depth implication part of one explicit chain.
deeper_reasoning_4.formal_sharpness: Tracks beta=(m/2)log2, nu<=1/3, the constant c_3<1/3, average total variation, and the Omega(log N) conclusion.
